subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-week-old infant is evaluated for poor feeding, hypotonia, and developmental delay. He has microcephaly, ptosis, a small jaw, syndactyly of the second and third toes, and ambiguous genitalia. Plasma cholesterol is 52 mg/dL, 7-dehydrocholesterol is markedly elevated, and electrolytes, glucose, and ammonia are normal.
question: Decreased activity of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible for this presentation?
explanation_correct: 7-Dehydrocholesterol reductase catalyzes the final step of cholesterol synthesis, the conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol. Its deficiency causes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, characterized by low plasma cholesterol, accumulation of 7-dehydrocholesterol, microcephaly, syndactyly, hypotonia, and ambiguous genitalia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Reduced HMG-CoA reductase activity would lower cholesterol without causing accumulation of 7-dehydrocholesterol, and statin-treated patients do not develop this malformation syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.B: Mevalonate kinase deficiency causes recurrent fevers and arthralgias with mevalonic aciduria, not dysmorphic features with 7-dehydrocholesterol accumulation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Squalene synthase acts upstream of the sterol ring intermediates, so its deficiency would not produce a selective rise in 7-dehydrocholesterol.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase initiates bile acid synthesis; its impairment causes cholestatic liver disease rather than this malformation pattern.

educationalObjective: Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome results from 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase deficiency, with low cholesterol, elevated 7-dehydrocholesterol, microcephaly, syndactyly, and ambiguous genitalia.
